Impact

Governments helping each other

This group was built to be a trusted space where governments can share questions and discuss solutions that can help them manage their natural resources for the greatest national benefit. Member countries offer each other help and receive expert advice to develop and implement policies which are context-appropriate, evidence-based, and transition proof.

We believe that reform and change gain better acceptance if led by producer countries. Problems and solutions are defined locally. Governments learn from each other and collaborate to develop practical tools to support policy implementation.

How we work

We don’t dictate policy; we facilitate the “policy labs” where national strategies are forged.

Our unique approach

Neutral Convening

A safe, non-commercial space for frank exchange.

Inter-Agency Labs

Bringing Energy, Environment, and Finance ministries together to align national strategy.

Peer-to-Peer Mentorship

Directly pairing producers to share practitioners’ experience.

A technical Help Desk that responds to live regulatory and negotiation challenges.

Guidelines · 4th edition · 2026 Guidelines for Good Governance in Emerging Oil and Gas ProducersValerie Marcel · Beth Mitchell NP4SE
Report · Jul 2026

Guidelines for Good Governance in Emerging Oil and Gas Producers 2026 (4th Edition)

Ten years on from the last edition, New Producers for Sustainable Energy (NP4SE) is pleased to share the fourth edition of its Guidelines for Good Governance in Emerging Oil and Gas Producers.

The recommendations are organised around eight core objectives, mapped against four key stages of resource development, so that officials can draw out the guidance most relevant to where their country actually sits — from pre-discovery through to long-term production.

This edition reflects a genuinely collaborative process. It draws on the consensus insights and strategies developed over a decade of annual meetings, technical workshops, and direct country engagements, and benefited substantially from the review and input of 27 officials from NP4SE member countries and knowledge partners, whose comments and suggestions shaped its final form.
